precepts.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: give them warning from me. If the watchman does not warn the wicked from his wicked way, the wicked man dies in his iniquity, but his blood will I require at thine hand. As teachers we do not even have a choice: if we do not tell you what you are doing wrong, that blood is on our hands.
precepts.point: Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me. God commands the prophets to go and show the people their sinful deeds.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

precepts.text: Had I sent thee to them of a strange speech, they would have hearkened unto thee.
precepts.point: The ox knoweth his owner, but Israel doth not know. Ask the nations who they are and they know their village; Israel gives a hundred answers.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” The Israelites are the only people on the face of the earth who do not know who they are. Ask around and you get a million answers: black, colored, African-American, Nuwabian, the Asiatic black man, Muslim, Christian, we are all one in Christ. Ask a white man and he is Polish; others can trace their lineage back to the village their ancestors came from.

“my people doth not consider”: not only do we not know who we are, we do not even consider that we could be the people of this book. We have been teaching it for forty years, and now there are urban apologists whose whole life is set around proving us wrong. We are the only people who will fight not to be God’s chosen. On a show like The Bachelor all the nations would run to be the bride of Christ, with the promises and the covenant; black people are the only ones saying, Don’t nobody want him.

Ezekiel shows it: “Not to many people of a strange speech and of an hard language, whose words thou canst not understand. Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.” God did not send the prophet to a people of a hard language. If he had, they would have hearkened in a heartbeat.

That is how we know we are the people. We have the best videos, the best music, the best teachers; the Bishops and Deacons broke the book down precept upon precept from the first book to Revelation, as no pastor in the history of Christianity ever touched, and still the negro says, Nah, I’m good, what about John 3:16? The other nations would hearken. Israel doth not know and doth not consider.

precepts.text: The house of Israel will not hearken unto thee, for they are impudent and hardhearted; fear them not, though they be a rebellious house.
precepts.point: The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Moses answered, “they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice”. Moses knew the spirit of his people, and the word to Ezekiel says it plainly.

“Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them. For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, but to the house of Israel”. Then: “Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee. But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.”

Israel is impudent, hardhearted and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept. So the Lord made Ezekiel's face strong against their faces: “fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.” That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

Israel in captivity today is the same impudent, hardhearted house that Moses knew, and that stubbornness is a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations.

A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning. That is the witness of Leviticus 5:1: he has seen or known of it, and he must utter it. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. If you know and say nothing, your brother’s blood is required because you did nothing about it.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Balak charged Balaam with blessing his enemies altogether, and Balaam answered, “Must I not take heed to speak that which the Lord hath put in my mouth?” That is the same charge given to Ezekiel.

“And he said unto me, Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them.” It is what every man must do who speaks on behalf of the Most High, especially the brothers: go unto the house of Israel and speak with His words unto them, not our own.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Balaam had to take heed to speak what the Lord put in his mouth, and the man sent to Israel must do the same, because of who he is sent to. “But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.”

So the Lord makes the face and forehead strong, meaning the mind: “Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads. As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.” Whatever excuse the people raise, He gives an answer through the scriptures on the spot.

The rebellious spirits on our people are only cast down by the word of God, which is why we speak what the Lord puts in our mouth, as Balaam had to.

precepts.text: When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, his righteousness shall not be remembered, and he shall die in his sin, exactly as it went for Joash.
precepts.point: Amaziah his son reigned in his stead; the fuller record of Joash is written in the story of the book of the kings.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“When a righteous man doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumblingblock before him, he shall die”, and “his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered.” He shall die in his sin. That is exactly how it went for Joash.

Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada’s guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols. But after he was warned he turned to wickedness and killed Zechariah, and none of that good was remembered in the end.

So judgment came: “For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the Lord delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash.” They left him “in great diseases”, and “his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed.” He was buried “in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings.”

Moses understood that life is temporary. Why enjoy it in sin when you’re going to get cast into the lake of fire, destroyed when the Son of God returns? Why do that? He said no, I’d rather suffer with my people.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

precepts.why:
Some think they have a choice, so Jeremiah 1. The words of Jeremiah came “in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign”, on to Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, “unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

Then the word of the Lord came: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”. Before I formed thee means before your mother was even pregnant, before you were in your mother’s womb, God knew you. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: before your mother gave birth, God sanctified you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

A leader’s, a prophet’s destiny is chosen for him. Your destiny was chosen for you; you cannot choose your own destiny. God ordained you a prophet. That is why, whether our people will hear or whether they will forbear, we have no choice but to go and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God.

Though they be a rebellious house: Israel is a rebellious house, and we are called to be revolutionaries, to be strong. When you examine the revolutionaries, they were all strong and prepared to be imprisoned for what they were doing for their community.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: The watchman must give warning. Staying silent to spare feelings would leave the wicked to die in their sins.

Today your church ministers, your mothers, your fathers have forgotten Jerusalem, their right hand has forgotten her cunning, and their tongue cleaves to the roof of their mouth, so that they're no longer a reprover: they're not speaking the laws of God.

note.label: By the Rivers of Babylon

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: Ezekiel is sent to the house of Israel, not to a people of strange speech and a hard language whose words he could not understand.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: Had the Most High sent him to such a people they would have hearkened, but the house of Israel will not hearken to Ezekiel because they will not hearken unto the Most High, for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The Most High makes Ezekiel's face and forehead strong against their faces, as an adamant harder than flint, so he need not fear them nor be dismayed at their looks though they be a rebellious house.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: He is to receive all the words in his heart, hear with his ears, and go to them of the captivity and speak, telling them "Thus saith the Lord GOD," whether they hear or whether they forbear.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The spirit takes Ezekiel up and he hears behind him a great rushing voice, "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place," along with the noise of the wings of the creatures and the wheels.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The spirit lifts him and takes him away, and he goes in bitterness in the heat of his spirit, but the hand of the Most High is strong upon him; he comes to the captivity at Tel-abib by the river Chebar and sits astonished among them seven days.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: At the end of seven days the word of the Most High makes Ezekiel a watchman unto the house of Israel, charged to hear the word and give the people warning.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: If Ezekiel fails to warn the wicked, that wicked man dies in his iniquity but his blood is required at the watchman's hand; if he warns and the man turns not, the man dies but Ezekiel has delivered his own soul.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The same holds for a righteous man who turns to iniquity: if unwarned, he dies in his sin and his blood is required at the watchman's hand, but if warned and he sins not, he shall surely live and the watchman is delivered.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The hand of the Most High is upon Ezekiel and he is sent out into the plain, where the glory of the Most High stands as the glory he saw by the river Chebar, and he falls on his face.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: The spirit sets him on his feet and tells him to shut himself in his house, where they shall bind him with bands; the Most High makes his tongue cleave to the roof of his mouth so he is dumb and cannot be a reprover, until the Most High opens his mouth to say, "Thus saith the Lord GOD," for they are a rebellious house.

note.label: Ezekiel 3: The Watchman unto the House of Israel

points: Where it says make your face hard: understand what this is about so there are no misunderstandings, so nobody says, I thought this was just going to be a walk in the park.

“Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads.” Why? Because our people want to stay in sin. Sin is pleasurable, and you are interfering in their pleasure.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not.” Fear them not, because, just like we read in Acts 17:5, certain lewd fellows of the baser sort were raised up by the unbelieving Jews, in fear and threat of death.

“Neither be dismayed at their looks”: don’t be dismayed at their looks, because our people know how to give a screw face. “Though they be a rebellious house.” And that’s just our people; we didn’t even get to the white man coming on us yet.
Make no mistake about it: we look for the enemy, Esau, but our people are one of the biggest enemies, because of jealousy and hatred.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel”: go talk to my people, go warn my people. “And speak with my words unto them”: we are not supposed to be speaking whatever comes into our mind; we are supposed to speak out of this Bible. That is why we have to study and learn this Bible and have it in our spirit, so we can speak it.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, but to the house of Israel”: we are sent to our people. Whatever state, city, island, country or continent you go to, you are going to the Israelites; go find the Israelites. This is speaking of other nations, the Russians, the Chinese, the Greeks, the Portuguese, the Spaniards; though even among our own we have to learn how to deal with those who speak other languages, like Creole, and build them up. “Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee”: if he had sent you to the East Indians or the Arabs, they would have listened to God.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee”: the real Israelites don’t want to listen. We love partying, confusion, arguing, holding on to things. The Day of Atonement has passed, and leaders are going to be counselling people who bring up things that happened before it: that means they never forgave their brother or sister, so they are not going to be forgiven, thus saith the Lord. “For all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted”: we are stubborn and hardhearted.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces”: that is why we go to the highways and byways, to the concourse places and the openings in the streets, and go back and forth with our people, because we love them that much, trying to win them over and bring them to Christ. “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks”: we get threats back to back in the streets, people saying they want to kill us, and we continue to do this work. Our people hate the Bible and hate God while they call themselves Christians, and they want to kill us because we bring them the word of God, “though they be a rebellious house.”

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: go to the Israelites, those in captivity. When we go to these islands and these countries, we go to our people who don’t even know they are Israelites, who have been worshipping Cesare Borgia because the Jesuit priests and Roman Catholic priests went down there with Christianity, rosary beads and little green Bibles. We have to battle for their souls and tell them: you are the Israelites; you are in captivity on this island, in this country, because you broke God’s laws. A lot of people in America don’t realize it to this day: they say they are free while they pay income tax and taxes on their food.

Unto thy people: when you go to China you are not teaching the Chinese, and when we go to Africa we are not teaching Hamites. The Hamites are not our people; God made it plain and clear. Wherever we go, Mexico, South America, Central America, we are calling our people to repentance, back to God, whether Hamites are in the mix or not. It is our job to wake them up out of that deep sleep, that coma, to resuscitate them and bring them back to life. You brothers on the internet critiquing our videos could use that same power to teach somebody in the street.

“Speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear”: tell them what God says through the Bible. Our hands are clean: God sent us, we taught them, and we go back and revisit to build them up, because we are the prophets of God back on this earth again. We are not cowards; we are on a mission from the Heavenly Father, ambassadors of God sent to wake our people and do this work.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: These are basic scriptures everybody should know, good ones to pull out when you are out teaching, because our people hate to see us coming.

“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: the people who were enslaved, who went through the transatlantic slave trade or the sub-Saharan slave trade. “And speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God”: we don’t come out there with our own words. We always have a Bible when we go out and teach. The pastor comes up to us with nothing in his hand, not even the app open on his phone; we have the scriptures, the Bible open.
“Whether they will hear”: whether you want to hear it, “or whether they will forbear”: whether you don’t want to hear it.

This goes on all the time: people in the community hate us for trying to fix the community. At a rally in Buffalo, New York, a black woman went to the police on us: we want them gone, they come down here to stir up this mess, they are telling us to hate white people. She was trying to get the police to stop us exercising our freedom of speech. We don’t tell nobody to hate white people. We may say God said he loved Jacob and hated Esau, but nobody in purple and gold teaches that you have to hate white people to get into the kingdom; that is a damn lie. She said don’t tell me something from 1300 years ago, but the Bible says to remember the days of old. How is she at a protest trying to fix the problem when she doesn’t even want to look into the days of old? And it is always the black woman with the bullhorn, trying to lead instead of letting the men of God lead. She said she puts her pants on just like they do; that lets you know she is destroyed. We pray these sisters repent and wake up and understand that what we are doing is the right thing. She said by the way we stand we are not with the community; so how we stand, not what we say, decides whether we are with the community.

Then at camp in Nashville a young woman jumped out of a car at the gas station where we were teaching, waving a Glock with an extended clip at the people in another car. The brother holding post saw the gun and called eyes up. The first thing was to spring into action and de-escalate with the word of God, because all she had to do was squeeze the trigger and somebody would lose their life: sister, think about your family, you have kids, don’t throw your life away for nothing, do not hate your brothers and sisters in your heart, God loves you. She acted like she wasn’t listening, but she heard the word of God. The man with her was just going to let it go down, ready to drive off and become an accessory and throw his life away too, until he was told to break it up. Then he had something to say: y’all stay in y’all lane. That is our lane: we are out there teaching, and it is our lane to protect the community with the word of God. We are not going to jump in and break them up; we let judgment be rendered on whoever God wants to render it on, but we use the word of God to calm it down. They ended up talking it out and nobody got shot or killed. We potentially stopped a murder, and still black women, pastors and black men say they don’t want us out there.

Our presence is needed. We can’t be in all places at all times, but we are going to be wherever the Lord needs us to be. This is the guide to fixing the broken people: we have to hit the streets and get boots on the ground. If you are just an internet prophet or social media prophet in our comments telling us how you would do it, typing two or three paragraphs nobody sees, be ashamed of yourself. Throw your keyboard away and get out on the streets with us on the front line, where the gunfire is. All that profound knowledge, and you ain’t teaching nobody. Be quiet, sit back and enjoy the ride, and if you don’t repent, enjoy the fire when it comes.

note.label: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

points: Why do we march on the churches and blitz Christianity? Because God commanded us to. “Go, get thee to them of the captivity”: the same way we were captive in ancient Babylon, our people are captive here in mystery Babylon. “Unto the children of thy people”: we are not going to the Arabs; we go to the children of our people.

“Speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they want to hear or not, whether they change or not, our job is to tell them thus saith the Lord and warn them. Some say the Christians will not get it, they are not of the elect; but you don’t know who is of the elect, and some of them change and come to the school.

Our job is not to hold hands and get along with all religions. It is to destroy every lie any religion pushes. It is not okay to be a Muslim and it is not okay to follow Christianity; we cast it down with the word of God and show why it is wrong. White Christianity is white supremacy and a lie.

note.label: RACIAL IDOLATRY: RACISM & PATRIOTISM

Most of the time the people do not want to hear, but “hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.” Our job is to warn our people to come out from the lies being taught on the earth.

note.label: RACIAL IDOLATRY: RACISM & PATRIOTISM

points: “When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die”: those in Christianity will die, because they are worshipping Satan, the beast; the Muslims need to come out of that, otherwise they die. “And thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life”: what we are trying to do is save lives. When we went out to the 2819 Church, we were out there to warn the wicked.

“The same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.” If we don’t warn the wicked, God will judge us, and we are not getting the kingdom. That goes for the Israelites who sit behind a computer and warn nobody, and for the scary ones who say we are making it hot and the government will come against us. We are here to turn this world upside down and cast down every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God. Many of us will go to jail, some will be put to death, exiled or deported; that is what we signed up for.

The dragon is wroth, and he is not coming for us alone but for all the Israelite camps. Many of them are already preparing to sell out and go back to being Negroes, shaving their beards and wearing detachable fringes, which are signs of weakness; fringes go on the garment, not snapped on a belt buckle. As 2 Esdras 16 says, then you shall know who is my chosen: when things get real, you will see who God’s real chosen are.

note.label: RACIAL IDOLATRY: RACISM & PATRIOTISM

points: “Speak with my words unto them”: as men and women of the Lord we are to use God’s words when we teach and when we speak. That’s what we’re supposed to do.

points: “Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads”: we are to make our minds strong against the minds of our rebellious brothers and sisters, male and female alike. This is how I was brought up, this is how the deacons and the captains were brought up, and you brothers in the Men of Valor program are going to be built up the same way. Do y’all realize we are at war? All nations are against us. So we are going to be strong against the evil; I don’t care how much we love you, once we see you are a snake we are going to come hard against you.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

points: “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead”: some of y’all come into this truth thinking this is church, like the Baptist church, where you can gossip and slander and it’s all good in Jesus, because you don’t believe that we are the nation of Israel. Some of you believe you are Haitians, Jamaicans or Afro-Americans, and you will die under them titles. The Lord is looking for Israelites.

points: “Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.” If God had sent us to another nation, they would have heard us. But God sent us to the Israelites.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.” Our people are hard-headed, and the job is not going to be easy, but we chose to do the job. There was a time that was us; we were hard-headed too, and now, praise the Messiah, we are here today.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads.” Our people have a hard face, especially Judah; when you go to talking to Judah, they look like they want to kill you. God has made your forehead harder than theirs. Don’t be afraid of that face; they aren’t going to do anything.

“As an adamant harder than flint”: adamant is something really, really hard, and it also means refusing to be persuaded or to change one’s mind. God gave Israel the power over this Bible. Whatever IUIC says the scripture says, that is what it says, and we do not care about the opinions of the apologetics and the other camps. We don’t care about your opinion, just like God don’t give a damn about your opinion. The scripture says one wife, one husband, and that is what we teach. You can go out and find a hundred scriptures and have as many hoes as you want; we don’t care. That is what the prophets in IUIC say, and God don’t care about anything else.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: the children of thy race. Read with verse 7, the children of thy people are the house of Israel. God did not send us to other nations; he sent us to the house of Israel. A little kid can see it, yet grown ass men who claim they went to school, to so-called seminary school, cannot understand this. This is for you dumb Christians.
Why “them of the captivity”? History shows we are the only people who went into slavery on slave cargo ships. We did not come here voluntarily. We are the captives, the children of the captivity.
“And speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” We, the leaders, the teachers, the prophets, the apostles, have no choice.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel”. We are the watchmen. The watchman watches for danger, and our job is to warn our people what is coming so they can prepare themselves.

We are watchmen over the house of Israel. Our responsibility is only to our people; our people come first. The Chinese love their own people and nobody calls them racist; Donald Trump makes it clear he only cares about his people and nobody calls him racist. When the Israelite says he only cares about his people, everybody says, you’re racist. Well, hell, be it then: I’m racist then, because the truth is I don’t give a damn about nobody else but my people. That does not mean not helping a child about to be hit by a car; it means my people come first. Everybody else cares about their own nation; y’all dumb Christians, something is wrong with y’all.

“Therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.” The word of God’s mouth is this Bible. When we open the Bible we give our brothers and sisters warning of what is coming: repent, for the kingdom of God is at hand; keep the law.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life”. Our job is to go to the wicked and tell the wicked to repent and leave his wicked ways, to save his life.
